newsitem.title: GERMANY: Iran blasts "false witness" in Berlin trial.
newsitem.headline: Iran blasts "false witness" in Berlin trial.

text.p: Iran described an Iranian exile as a "false witness" as he testified in camera on Friday for a second day at the trial of five men accused of carrying out political killings on Tehran's orders.
The Berlin court ruled that the man was in grave danger and it barred the media and public to protect his identity when he began his evidence on Thursday.
His name was put forward by the prosecution's star witness, exiled former Iranian president Abolhassan Banisadr, at the nearly three-year trial of four Lebanese and one Iranian.
The court and prosecutors described the man as a former Iranian state official who fled after being sentenced to death. Banisadr said he used to work for the Iranian secret service.
The Iranian embassy in Bonn issued a statement saying that the man was an imposter and could only bear false witness if he claimed to be an ex-security official for Iran.

"Not one single member of the security service of the Islamic Republic of Iran has ever abandoned the country. Any personal papers, which claim any such identity, should be regarded as having been forged," it said.

But lawyers representing the familes of three exiled Iranian Kurdish leaders and their translator, who were killed in a hail of bullets in September 1992, said the man's testimony was "well-informed" and "impressive."
A lawyer representing the victims' relatives, Axel Jeschke, said: "The witness knows what he is talking about." Another lawyer said that he had made an "excellent impression."
The five defendants are charged planning and carrying out the 1992 machinegun killings in the Berlin restaurant Mykonos.
Banisadr told the court in August that Iran's religious leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, ordered the killings and President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani signed the order.
Banisadr cited the alleged Iranian defector as one of his sources and prosecutors say the man's inside knowledge means his life would be in danger if he were identified.
